flux_evidence: The base model itself is frozen, but the downstream ecosystem moved concretely this cycle: OneTrainer merged support, a community 2.9B fork got a LoRA-compatibility fix and an upstream sd-scripts PR, a new official Turbo v1.1 checkpoint shipped, and the base-vs-finetune download race flipped — all within about two weeks of the 2026-08-22 check.

findings.claim: references/lora-training.md's trainer table says: "OneTrainer | No Anima support found either way. Check its changelog before planning around it".
findings.reality: OneTrainer merged native Anima support on 2026-07-04 (PR #1487 "New model: Anima", gated behind the diffusers Cosmos pipeline landing). The tracking issue Nerogar/OneTrainer#1278 was closed as completed the same window.
findings.fix_hint: references/lora-training.md trainer table ~L45 — replace the OneTrainer row with confirmed support (merged 2026-07-04) and note it's the only trainer with genuine validation loss, which bears directly on the contested character-LoRA-difficulty claim nearby.

findings.claim: SKILL.md ~L241 / two-bar bullet ~L260 and references/setup-and-workflows.md ~L115 treat whether Anima-Base LoRAs load on the Anima-2.9B fork as an open, unanswered question (u/Neonsea1234's post went unanswered).
findings.reality: It's now answered and documented: loading a Base LoRA as-is on 2.9B silently corrupts identity (0/3 success, ComfyUI gives no warning) because layer insertion shifts block numbers; remapping the LoRA's block keys to the new numbering restores it (3/3). Separately, kohya-ss/sd-scripts PR #2418 ("Add support for expanded Anima 2.9B model by detecting block count from keys", open non-draft, last updated 2026-08-14) is upstream work toward native support — evidence the fork is gaining traction rather than staying a footnote.
findings.fix_hint: SKILL.md ~L241 and two-bar bullet ~L260; references/setup-and-workflows.md ~L115 — replace "assumes not" framing with: LoRAs don't load directly (silent corruption) but do work with block-key remapping; the fork now has upstream sd-scripts interest, so it's no longer purely a footnote.

findings.claim: SKILL.md ~L23/52 and setup-and-workflows.md ~L211 state "A community checkpoint already out-downloads the official base — MiaoMiao Harem at ~199k against ~190k [2026-08-22]", framing Anima like SDXL where most people run a finetune.
findings.reality: As of 2026-09-09 the official Anima listing's total downloads (218,777, all versions) now edge past MiaoMiao Harem's total (215,667). More importantly the comparison was apples-to-oranges: MiaoMiao Harem is a multi-base checkpoint (Anima + Illustrious + NoobAI + Pony); only its Anima-tagged versions sum to ~102.6k downloads, well under Anima-Base alone (89,433) plus Aesthetic/Turbo. A same-base comparison shows the official checkpoints clearly ahead, not behind.
findings.fix_hint: SKILL.md ~L23 blockquote and ~L52; references/setup-and-workflows.md ~L211 — drop the "out-downloads" framing or replace with the corrected, same-base comparison; the SDXL analogy may need softening since it rests on this now-reversed number.

findings.claim: SKILL.md variant table ~L46 lists only Anima-Turbo v1.0 (`anima-turbo-v1.0.safetensors`).
findings.reality: CircleStone shipped anima-turbo-v1.1.safetensors (uploaded by tdrussell) alongside Aesthetic v1.1; it already has ~16,886 Civitai downloads and community notes describe it as improving on v1.0's flatness and detail expression.
findings.fix_hint: SKILL.md variant table ~L46 — add the v1.1 row/note, parallel to how Aesthetic v1.1 is already flagged as undocumented-in-card.

findings.claim: The watchlist and SKILL.md ~L45 say no vendor CFG figure exists for Aesthetic and the skill's number is extrapolated from Base.
findings.reality: The official card still doesn't document Aesthetic v1.1 or give it a CFG figure, but community sources now converge on CFG ~3 for Aesthetic ("tolerates lower CFGs such as 3, and often looks better with them"), which is lower than Base's 4-5.
findings.fix_hint: SKILL.md ~L45 and references/setup-and-workflows.md — the extrapolated CFG 4 could be replaced with the community-sourced ~3, tagged `[community]` since it's still not official.

findings.claim: The watchlist flags animastyles.thetacursed.com as a volatile mirror URL at risk of going dead after ThetaCursed's GitHub was suspended.
findings.reality: The site resolves fine and still advertises 40,000+ artist tags; the source GitHub repo (github.com/ThetaCursed/Anima-Style-Explorer) is live with an index file named for 59k artists, suggesting the count has grown past what the skill cites.
findings.fix_hint: references/prompting-guide.md ~L102 — no urgent fix needed; optionally bump the artist count from 42k+ to the newer 59k figure once confirmed against the live site's own count.

new_techniques.what: To use an Anima-Base LoRA on the community Anima-2.9B fork (28→40 layers via LLaMA-Pro-style expansion), remap the LoRA's block-number keys using the layer-insertion position table before loading; loading as-is silently misapplies deltas to the wrong blocks (0/3 success) while remapped keys work (3/3).
new_techniques.why_it_matters: Without this, ComfyUI loads a mismatched LoRA with no warning and quietly corrupts character identity, which is exactly the kind of silent-failure trap this skill documents elsewhere.

new_techniques.what: A Civitai sd-scripts guide gives per-type Anima LoRA settings: character (dim/alpha 8, lr 1e-4, 1000-1500 steps, 20-30 images), multi-outfit character (lr 1e-3 then 5e-5 refine, ~900+ steps/outfit), style (dim/alpha 16, lr 5e-5, 6500 steps, 60-150 images), concept (dim/alpha 4-8, lr 1e-4, 1200-2000 steps).
new_techniques.why_it_matters: Gives named, reproducible numbers where the skill currently states a single generic recipe (2e-5 LR at rank 32) with no type-specific breakdown; it directly bears on the contested character-LoRA-difficulty watchlist item.

new_techniques.what: kohya-ss/sd-scripts PR #2418 adds automatic detection of Anima-2.9B's expanded block count from checkpoint keys, moving toward native trainer-side support for the layer-expanded fork rather than manual handling.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: Signals the community fork is being absorbed into mainline tooling rather than staying an experimental footnote, which should update the fork's current "not for production" framing.

new_techniques.what: CircleStone shipped anima-turbo-v1.1.safetensors, an update to the Turbo distillation, alongside Aesthetic v1.1.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: It's a new default-candidate checkpoint in the Turbo-vs-Aesthetic contest the skill already flags as unresolved, and isn't in the variant table at all yet.

add.claim: Turbo v1.1 exists but is undocumented in the skill and its relationship to the contested Turbo-vs-Aesthetic default is unassessed.
add.check: Check whether the model card documents v1.1's changes and whether community opinion on the Turbo-vs-Aesthetic default shifts once v1.1 is accounted for.

amend.note: LoRA-compat question is now answered (fails as-is, works with block-key remap) and sd-scripts PR #2418 shows upstream interest in native 2.9B support — the fork is no longer a pure footnote; re-check whether it should get variant-selector treatment.

Re-sampled 2026-09-09: official Anima total downloads (218,777) now edge past MiaoMiao Harem's total (215,667), and the original comparison mixed MiaoMiao Harem's non-Anima base-model versions in; use same-base download figures going forward.
Community now cites CFG ~3 for Aesthetic (still not on the official card), and Turbo v1.1 shipped, complicating the existing v1.0 Turbo-vs-Aesthetic framing.
